candidate_validity_model.candidate: a candidate is a durable canonical record set (a Subject aggregate or its owned records) that can be enumerated deterministically from authoritative bootstrap input, the durable record set, or deterministic projections; candidates are never invented, ranked, or guessed
candidate_validity_model.validity_rule: a candidate is valid iff ALL of the allowed validity filters pass: correct project/workflow scope, canonical record type present, valid lineage, valid predecessor for the intended operation, explicit materialized Decision basis when the operation is decision-backed, authority eligibility under M3-A2 typed authority, and revision compatibility under M3-A3 expected/current revision semantics
candidate_validity_model.many_to_one_rule: no hidden reduction of a many-candidate set to one: if the deterministic validity filter leaves more than one valid candidate, the result is MANY (NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE); no recency/newest, similarity, nearest-timestamp, path-proximity, or first-match tie-break is ever applied to reduce many to one
candidate_validity_model.determinism: the validity evaluation is a pure deterministic function of durable state: identical durable state always yields the identical candidate set and the identical zero/one/many result

zero_one_many_rule.computation_order: candidate validity is evaluated deterministically FIRST; the count (zero/one/many) is computed only after the deterministic validity filter (CANDIDATE_COUNT_COMPUTED_AFTER_DETERMINISTIC_VALIDITY_FILTER=yes); no heuristic pre-filter ever runs (HEURISTIC_PRE_FILTER_ALLOWED=no)

ZERO.definition: no valid candidate remains after the deterministic validity filter
results: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND: no durable Subject matches the canonical identity/lineage at all
PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE: a durable Subject exists but the projection/index is stale or missing; recovery may rebuild the projection from durable records
missing prerequisite evidence: required authority / revision / predecessor / Decision evidence is absent; bounded explicit error (failure_policy)
NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: no valid candidate but semantically distinct possibilities exist that only an explicit human/LLM choice can disambiguate
ZERO.never: a fake Subject is never created to satisfy a zero result: ZERO never fabricates identity, never guesses a parent, and never invents a Subject

ONE.definition: exactly one valid candidate remains after the deterministic validity filter
requirements: materialized semantic basis: the candidate's semantic Decision is durably materialized (semantic_decision_materialization)
required authority valid: M3-A2 typed authority eligibility holds
required revision/predecessor valid: M3-A3 expected/current revision and predecessor-state validation hold
ONE.automation: automatic binding/recovery proceeds iff candidate_count==1 AND the materialized Decision basis exists AND the required authority is valid AND the required revision/predecessor is valid; otherwise NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE or a bounded deterministic not-found/conflict (SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTOMATION_RULE)

MANY.definition: more than one valid candidate remains after the deterministic validity filter

zero_one_many_rule.SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTOMATION_RULE: automatic binding/recovery iff candidate_count==1 AND candidate semantic decision durably materialized AND required authority valid AND required revision/predecessor valid. Otherwise NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE or a bounded deterministic not-found/conflict. HEURISTIC_SUBJECT_SELECTION_ALLOWED=no.

decision_requirements: a canonical Decision record exists in the durable record set
the Decision belongs to the correct owning Subject (A1 exactly-one ownership)
the Decision explicitly authorizes the relevant followup category
the Decision is not superseded or invalid

authority_engine_boundary.rule: the Authority Engine mechanically verifies that the Decision exists, is owned by the correct Subject, explicitly authorizes the relevant followup category, is not superseded/invalid, and has deterministic lineage; it never infers intent, never selects semantics, and never creates the Decision

semantic_decision_materialization.rule: a unique candidate is never sufficient by itself: decision-backed binding/recovery requires a durably materialized Decision that passes every decision_requirement (A3 AUTHORITY_ENGINE_MAY_VERIFY_MATERIALIZED_DECISION=yes preserved)

binding_kinds.rule: binding kinds are defined separately with per-kind rules; a single generic algorithm without per-kind rules is forbidden

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: durable Subject aggregates under the correct project/workflow scope, deterministically enumerated from authoritative records
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical record type present; valid lineage; valid predecessor for the intended operation; authority eligibility; revision compatibility; no recency/newest, title/text similarity, nearest timestamp, path proximity, first match, or LLM similarity signals
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND / PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE / missing prerequisite evidence / NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE; never a fake Subject
kinds.ONE_RESULT: unique candidate alone is insufficient; requires materialized Decision basis (when decision-backed), valid required authority, and valid required revision/predecessor; otherwise NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE or bounded deterministic conflict
kinds.MANY_RESULT: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE; no automatic selection and no heuristic tie-break

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: the explicit parent Subject reference carried by the materialized Decision (source_decision_ref); child candidates are existing FollowupEdge + child Subject records under that parent
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical Decision exists, is owned by the parent Subject, explicitly authorizes the followup category, is not superseded/invalid, and has deterministic lineage; parent aggregate CAS valid (A3 followup transaction); child creation requires FORBIDDEN_CHILD_WITHOUT_VERIFIED_DECISION=no violation
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: child absent: materialize exactly once via the A3 followup transaction on the verified Decision basis; never a fake or guessed child
kinds.ONE_RESULT: exactly one existing child with a verified Decision basis: reconcile/return the existing child (idempotent recovery); never create a second child
kinds.MANY_RESULT: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: multiple children claiming the same Decision basis require an explicit choice

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: the durable Subject aggregate referenced by the Execution record's explicit subject_ref
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical Execution record type; subject_ref points to an existing Subject aggregate with valid lineage; authority eligibility; revision compatibility; no heuristic signals
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND (orphan Execution): bounded explicit error; recovery may resolve only via deterministic index repair, never by guessing a Subject
kinds.ONE_RESULT: bind to the exactly-one referenced Subject after all requirements hold; unique alone is insufficient
kinds.MANY_RESULT: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: multiple Subject aggregates claim the same Execution

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: the durable Subject aggregate referenced by the Completion record's explicit subject_ref
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical Completion record type; explicit subject_ref to an existing Subject aggregate with valid lineage; authority eligibility; revision compatibility; no heuristic signals
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND / missing prerequisite evidence; never a fake Subject
kinds.ONE_RESULT: bind/reconcile to the exactly-one referenced Subject after all requirements hold; unique alone is insufficient
kinds.MANY_RESULT: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: multiple Subject aggregates claim the same Completion

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: durable review/result records with an explicit subject_ref to a Subject aggregate
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical review/result record type; explicit subject_ref to an existing Subject aggregate with valid lineage; authority eligibility; revision compatibility; acceptance of the review itself is never automated
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND / missing prerequisite evidence; never a fake Subject
kinds.ONE_RESULT: bind/reconcile to the exactly-one referenced Subject after all requirements hold; the review acceptance semantic remains a human/LLM materialized Decision, never auto-accepted
kinds.MANY_RESULT: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: multiple Subject aggregates claim the same review/result
kinds.AUTOMATION_ALLOWED: yes_only_when_one_valid_candidate_and_all_requirements_hold; review acceptance itself is never automated

kinds.CANDIDATE_SOURCE: PlanSubject / WorkSubject records within the correct project/workflow scope
kinds.VALIDITY_RULE: canonical record type; correct project/workflow scope; valid lineage; valid predecessor; materialized Decision basis when decision-backed; authority eligibility; revision compatibility; no heuristic signals
kinds.ZERO_RESULT: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND / PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE / missing prerequisite evidence / NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE
kinds.ONE_RESULT: bind when the automation rule holds (one valid candidate + materialized Decision + valid authority + valid revision/predecessor); unique alone is insufficient

recovery_boundary.definition: recovery is the bounded, deterministic read-then-repair process that re-establishes correct binding/projection state from durable authority; it never performs semantic reasoning

BINDING_VS_RECOVERY.binding: selecting and binding a Subject from candidates when the SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTOMATION_RULE holds (candidate_count==1 AND materialized Decision AND valid authority AND valid revision/predecessor); otherwise NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE or bounded deterministic not-found/conflict
BINDING_VS_RECOVERY.recovery: repairing deterministic projection/index/pointer state and replaying idempotent projections over durable records; recovery may bind a uniquely determined already-decided followup but never chooses semantics

may: rebuild a stale projection from the durable record set
bind a uniquely determined already-decided followup
recovery_boundary.bounded: every recovery action is bounded by durable records and explicit references; unbounded search, similarity search, and semantic ranking are forbidden

projection_recovery.stale_subject_rule: a stale current pointer or stale projection never hides a durable Subject: the Subject remains visible and enumerable from the durable record set; the projection may be rebuilt from durable records
projection_recovery.no_escalation_for_rebuild: diagnosing or rebuilding a stale projection never requires a SPEC / Profile Task / Plan / Work Item escalation: read-only inspection and projection rebuild are mechanical operations over durable records
projection_recovery.rebuild_source: projections rebuild deterministically from the committed durable record set only; current pointers, event logs, and git history are never projection sources of authority
projection_recovery.drift_repair: deterministic index/projection drift is repaired by re-derivation from durable records; the durable record set is never modified by projection repair

readonly_diagnostic_exemption.capability_lease_exception: a capability lease is required ONLY when the operation itself requires bounded privileged access unrelated to lifecycle mutation (e.g., a genuinely privileged host/runtime operation); no lifecycle mutation, binding, or projection access is ever part of that requirement
readonly_diagnostic_exemption.independent_availability: safe Host/runtime/git/project inspection is independently available without Subject binding and without lifecycle mutation (A2 READONLY_DIAGNOSTIC_PLANE_PRESERVED=yes preserved)
readonly_diagnostic_exemption.no_forced_artifacts: safe read-only diagnosis creates no forced Plan / Work Item / SPEC / Profile Task / approval / followup

conflicts.meaning: zero valid candidates and no durable Subject matches the canonical identity/lineage
conflicts.notes: distinct from PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE: a missing Subject is not a stale projection

conflicts.meaning: more than one valid candidate (or otherwise undecidable binding); equivalent to NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE
conflicts.notes: no heuristic tie-break, no hidden many->one reduction

conflicts.meaning: many valid candidates, or a unique candidate missing a required semantic basis; exactly one explicit human/LLM choice is required
conflicts.notes: the canonical ambiguous outcome of zero_one_many_rule

conflicts.meaning: the candidate's predecessor state is invalid for the intended operation
conflicts.notes: state legality, distinct from revision timing (M3-A3 PREDECESSOR_STATE_CONFLICT preserved)

conflicts.meaning: expected revision != current revision of the target aggregate at the CAS check (M3-A3 REVISION_CONFLICT semantics)
conflicts.notes: stale mutation fails closed; no merge, no last-write-wins

conflicts.meaning: the required M3-A2 typed authority is invalid or missing for the binding/recovery
conflicts.notes: identity alone never authorizes; a bare Subject ID is never authority

conflicts.meaning: decision-backed binding/recovery attempted without a durably materialized, valid Decision
conflicts.notes: unique candidate alone is insufficient; the Decision is never inferred

conflicts.meaning: a durable Subject exists but the projection/index is stale or missing; deterministic rebuild from durable records is available
conflicts.notes: the durable Subject remains visible; the stale pointer never hides it

conflict_taxonomy.canonical_distinct: every result code is canonical and distinct and never collapses into another result's error semantics (WCTX-1 pairwise distinct error taxonomy preserved)

revision_authority_relation.authoritative_mutation: authoritative mutation/materialization obeys the M3-A3 expected revision/CAS contract and the M3-A2 typed authority contract; binding/recovery never bypasses either
revision_authority_relation.read_only_resolution: read-only binding resolution may be non-mutating (projection reads) but never implies mutation authority: a read-only resolution grants no CAS, no lease, and no authorization to mutate
revision_authority_relation.authority_and_revision_required: automatic binding/recovery requires BOTH valid required authority AND valid required revision/predecessor (SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTOMATION_RULE)

idempotent_recovery.repeat_rule: repeated deterministic recovery of the same state produces the same/reconciled result and never duplicates a semantic effect
idempotent_recovery.existing_effect: when the canonical mechanical effect already exists, recovery returns the same/reconciled result and creates no second Subject and no second edge
idempotent_recovery.no_second_subject_or_edge: no second Subject and no second edge are ever created by recovery replay
idempotent_recovery.basis: A3 idempotency model preserved: durable dedupe metadata plus deterministic semantic fingerprints; recovery replay is request-layer replay over durable records

failure_policy.unsafe_mutation: fail closed: a mutation/recovery step whose preconditions cannot be mechanically verified fails closed before any authoritative write
failure_policy.safe_diagnosis: safe read-only diagnosis is always available and requires no Subject binding and no capability lease (readonly_diagnostic_exemption)
failure_policy.ambiguous_semantics: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: ambiguity is never resolved by heuristics, recency, similarity, or a silent default
failure_policy.missing_deterministic_prerequisite: bounded explicit error identifying the missing prerequisite (e.g., MATERIALIZED_DECISION_MISSING, SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTHORITY_DENIED, SUBJECT_BINDING_PREDECESSOR_INVALID, SUBJECT_BINDING_REVISION_CONFLICT)
failure_policy.no_blind_replay: blind replay with stale facts is denied; retry requires fresh validation (new authority evaluation, new expected revision) per M3-A3 retry_policy
failure_policy.never_invents: binding/recovery never invents data: no fake Subject, no invented Decision, no guessed parent

design_scenarios.NAME: one valid already-decided candidate: deterministic binding
design_scenarios.given: exactly one valid already-decided candidate after the deterministic validity filter, with a durably materialized Decision, valid required authority, and valid required revision/predecessor
design_scenarios.expected: SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTOMATION_RULE holds (candidate_count==1 AND materialized Decision AND valid authority AND valid revision/predecessor): deterministic binding proceeds; the binding is durable and revisioned per M3-A3

design_scenarios.NAME: two valid candidates: ambiguity fails closed
design_scenarios.given: the deterministic validity filter leaves two valid candidates for the same binding
design_scenarios.expected: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE (SUBJECT_AMBIGUOUS): no automatic selection, no heuristic tie-break, and no hidden reduction of the many-candidate set to one (NO_HIDDEN_REDUCTION_MANY_TO_ONE=yes)

design_scenarios.NAME: zero candidates: bounded not-found, no fabricated Subject
design_scenarios.given: a binding request whose deterministic validity filter leaves zero valid candidates
design_scenarios.expected: bounded zero-result: SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND (or the appropriate zero-result code from zero_one_many_rule.ZERO, including PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE or missing prerequisite evidence); no fabricated Subject and no fake Subject is ever created

design_scenarios.NAME: one candidate without a materialized Decision
design_scenarios.given: exactly one valid candidate but no durably materialized Decision basis exists
design_scenarios.when: the decision-backed followup binding operation runs
design_scenarios.expected: MATERIALIZED_DECISION_MISSING: no automatic followup binding occurs (UNIQUE_CANDIDATE_BYPASSES_MATERIALIZED_DECISION=no); the unique candidate alone is insufficient and the Decision is never inferred

design_scenarios.NAME: one candidate with stale revision: fail closed
design_scenarios.given: exactly one valid candidate but the expected revision is stale: the expected revision does not equal the current revision of the target aggregate
design_scenarios.expected: SUBJECT_BINDING_REVISION_CONFLICT: the stale expected revision does not equal the current revision of the target aggregate, so the binding mutation must fail closed (STALE_REVISION_MUTATION=fail_closed); no mutation and no binding commit occurs; retry requires fresh validation

design_scenarios.NAME: one candidate with invalid authority: denied
design_scenarios.given: exactly one valid candidate but the required M3-A2 typed authority is invalid or missing
design_scenarios.expected: SUBJECT_BINDING_AUTHORITY_DENIED: the binding is denied; the unique candidate does not bypass authority (UNIQUE_CANDIDATE_BYPASSES_AUTHORITY=no); identity alone never authorizes

design_scenarios.NAME: stale current pointer over a valid durable Subject
design_scenarios.given: a valid durable Subject exists but the current pointer / projection is stale or missing
design_scenarios.expected: PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE: the durable Subject remains discoverable from the durable record set and is never hidden by the stale pointer (STALE_POINTER_MUST_NOT_HIDE_DURABLE_SUBJECT=yes); the projection may be rebuilt deterministically; no SPEC/Profile Task escalation occurs merely to diagnose or rebuild

design_scenarios.NAME: safe read-only host diagnosis needs no binding
design_scenarios.expected: the operation completes with only host/environment evidence; no Subject binding, no capability lease, and no forced Plan / Work Item / SPEC / Profile Task / approval / followup is required (SAFE_READONLY_DIAGNOSIS_REQUIRES_SUBJECT_BINDING=no; SAFE_READONLY_DIAGNOSIS_REQUIRES_CAPABILITY_LEASE=no)

design_scenarios.NAME: a newer candidate is still ambiguous
design_scenarios.given: two valid candidates for the same binding, where one candidate is newer (recency differs)
design_scenarios.expected: still NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE: recency/newest is a forbidden signal (forbidden_validity_signals.recency_newest=forbidden), the newer candidate is never auto-selected, and the many-candidate set is never reduced to one

design_scenarios.NAME: recovery replay does not duplicate the semantic effect
design_scenarios.given: an already-materialized followup (child Subject + edge + verified Decision basis) and a recovery replay of the same deterministic recovery
design_scenarios.expected: the existing canonical mechanical effect returns the same/reconciled result; no second child Subject and no second edge are created (RECOVERY_REPLAY_DUPLICATES_SEMANTIC_EFFECT=no; IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY=must_not_duplicate_semantic_effects)
